package_info.package_manager: custom firmware (Linux-based, not a standard package manager)
package_info.package_versions: unspecified; affected versions use Linux kernel EOL 2016 and packages up to 23 years old
package_info.why_malicious: The firmware is not described as intentionally malicious, but it is built on severely outdated components with hundreds of critical vulnerabilities, creating a high risk of compromise. The lack of transparency and use of unsupported software exposes users to exploitation, which is a severe security concern.

behavioral_signatures: Bundling of software packages with known critical vulnerabilities
Lack of SBOM or transparency in component versions
file_indicators: Firmware images containing Linux kernel versions EOL before 2017
Presence of software packages with release dates >10 years old
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Analyze firmware images for embedded Linux kernel and package versions. Flag any firmware using EOL kernels or packages with known critical vulnerabilities. Require and review SBOMs for transparency. Use vulnerability scanners to enumerate and assess the risk of all included components.
